I can't speak highly enough about this game, it's a shame 2K Publishing didn't let Turtle Rock Studios really do what they wanted.
That said, this game creates such an exciting environment where either the lone Monster player, or group of four hunters, can be on the hunt for prey...or prey for the hunt.
This game takes SKILL to play well, but can still be a lot of fun if you have three friends to play with as hunters.
The hunters absolutely have to have good teamwork and communication, or they're at a disadvantage.
A monster only has to rely on themselves to win, but if the hunters play a solid game and don't make silly mistakes, the monster still has to earn the win. Which is a great feeling.
This game is not something you pickup playing with just a few games. There are multiple choices in hunter classes, different play styles, various monsters that all require their own sort of strategy to beat.
The complexity of the strategy and tactics, along with the chest pounding fights, escapes and hard fought battles is what makes this game amazing.
As a mostly monster player, the feeling of power and the thrill of the chase is intensely immserive and this game is now one of four that make me shake in excitement, with the other three being Counter-Strike, Tiberian Sun and Chess.  I believe PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS is going to be the fifth, but I need a better PC so I can play and find that out!

Everyone's been waiting for Nintendo to get around to making a new Metroid game since Metroid: Other M came out nearly 6 years ago. Unfortunately, it seems that the amazing series isn't worth reviving, which is a sad disappointment to fans of the series, myself included. Even if NIntendo did decide to revive the series, it would most likely be revamped into something that is unlike what we all know and love. So, you ask, how can I relive my childhood memories of searching for hidden items, exploring exotic worlds, fighting bizarre bosses unlike any I've ever seen. Well, look no further. Ladies and Gentlegamers, Axiom Verge is what you've been looking for.
The series starts you off with an elusive plot that introduces you to your main character, but is vague enough that it keeps you searching for answers for the next several hours of the game. You wake up in a strange egg-like structure, forced to begin making your way around. Despite the fact that it doesn't contian a near-silent protagonist like the classic Metroid games, Axiom Verge still manages to keep you in the dark with it's plot, slowly revealing pieces to you for a mind-blowing finale. The game is chock-full of interesting environments, creatures, and boss-fights that will give you a rush of adrenaline and nostalgia that you haven't probably felt since you beat Metroid Zero Mission a decade ago.
The best part of all is the replay value. Heck, you'll find yourself searching for all the hidden items and secrets scattered all over the map long after you've beaten the game's final boss. The game has a similar end-game bonus if you manage to get nearly all the items in the game, giving you a secret ending. The world also has several pieces of paper and tablets that reveal parts of the plot that aren't normally obtained during the main gameplay.
My only major gripe about the game is the keyboard layout. It's unlike any I've ever seen in a game, especially a platformer, and won't have you holding your mouse and your fingers on the WASD keys. For this reason, I highly recommend grabbing a controller if you've got one handy, if not, it takes a little while getting used to the layout, but it's by no means a deal-breaker.
So, I'm sure you're asking yourself, is this game merely a copy of Metroid? Will I just feel like I'm replaying Super Metroid, except now I'm out twenty bucks? Absolutely not. While Axiom Verge will tingle your nostalgia senses, but it's got it's own wonderfully crafted story and world that stands all on it's own.
Is it worth it? Heck freaking yes. I'm gonna stop writing so you can do yourself a favor and buy it.

Axiom verge is a throw back to the old NES/SNES Metroid style gameplay that some call Metroidvania that references Castlevania and Metroid.  It is a side scrolling shooter that plays about as fast as Metroid or Castlevania and can easily become difficult if you increase the difficulty.
The story is based on a scientist that has something go wrong in his lab and then he ends up elsewhere.  Without going further into the story, it gets unique to say the least.  You get a multitude of different weapons, one for each number key on your keyboard and a few secrets as well as abilities that enable you to access more parts of the level. Things like phase shifting through walls to upgraded weapon power and health nodes.
The graphics on the store page are what you get.  A retro throwback to the golden days of gaming.  As you explore the level you will find secrets in the walls as well as secret levels that give you more upgrades.  Overall, my play time logged is how long it took me to finish the game with most of everything collected.  You can speed run the game in a much quicker fashion if you like but you miss out on the exploration and the bosses can be considerbly harder without additional power or health increases.
My only complaint, is without hard mode, the bosses are incredibly easy to beat and can be cheesed with ease.  Even the final boss was relativelty easy.  As I have said before, this can be remedied with hard mode and can make things a bit more difficult and possibly frusterating.
For anyone looking at a side scrolling action platformer, I would recommend this game.  I couldn't pull myself away at times and wanted to keep on playing.  When a game does that to the player, it tends to show how well designed it is.  I hope there is a sequel planned, I had read talks about it but who knows.  The story was well designed and threw a curveball at me as I progressed, which is an awesome way to immerse the player.
The only negative things I can think of with this game that would detract and possible sway a purchase is that the bosses are indeed cheesable.  Even on hard, you can still cheese them but everything else is generally much more difficult.

Honestly, as a Reflex fan this game is a let down, but there are things I like about it, and things I absolutely hate!
HATE:
1.PRELOAD - Remove it from the game, it is like going backwards in the evolution of gaming, and has nothing to do with real life riding, as others have suggested just make it so you pull back to seat bounce. (like in real life!)
2.JUMP OFF THE STARTING LINE - Remove it from the game, he has enough boost using the clutch, why did you put such an UNREALISTIC start to the riders right when the gate drops?, it is like the rider is in a sling shot! Totally unrealistic!
3.TUFF BLOCKS OBJECT COLLISION - Modify this code, When you hit a TUFF BLOCK the rider just stops, like he has hit an invisible wall and he just stays straight, no angular collision movement and totally unrealistic consequences to running into this object, Reflex was way more believable!
4.CONTROLLER SETTINGS, FORCE FEEDBACK IS NOT AN OPTION - Fix it, give us the option to turn off game pad force feedback.
5.PHYSICS - THE WHIP - This is the biggest gripe I have about the game, put the REFLEX whip back into this game and you will have a major hit on your hands! The whip in this game is very dumb feeling and totally goes backwards in the evolution of this franchise.
Those are the MUST FIX for me, there are more but that would fix your game and would show respect to your future Target Market Fans.
LIKE:
1.CLUTCH action - Awesome!, at least it works and is more apparent than the reflex clutch which really does not work very well.
2.TRACKS - Awesome!
3.TEXTURES - Awesome! Visually, you guys really improved on this, I build tracks for reflex and I can really respect the advance in the texture quality, very real looking!
4.OBJECTS - Awesome! Visually very real looking!
5.GRAPHICS - Awesome! Game plays and looks great!

As a long time fan of the mx and mx vs atv games, I really am disappointed in this game. I remember watching a video of a dev talking about how they were using the reflex engine, yet here we are with an alive clone that plays like a crap mx game you'd download for free on your iphone.
I really want this game to go somewhere and not waste my 20 bucks, so I'll list things I find to be poorly done.
-So far I've played 3 races, after that I can't play more than 2-3 laps without the game shutting off. no crash message, nothing. Just ♥♥♥♥♥ off and goes to desktop.
-The AI is inconsistant as hell, theres times I'll easily put 5-10 seconds on the AI, then they randomly come out of nowhere and pass me, when I didn't make a mistake.
-The controls are sluggish feeling, it feels like something out of a game I played long ago, Big motha truckers. I don't want to feel like I'm driving a semi when I'm playing an MX game.
-When you jump, it feels like you slow down and just fall out of the air, that isn't how it works, and isn't how it should look/feel.
-Preloading feels more like a forward boost, using it in the woops section effectively turns you into a superhero. If you fix the problem stated previously of slowing down and falling out of the air, you wouldn't need the forward boost to make the jumps in a preload, just the upward boost.
-The wheelies make me sad. If you don't know what I mean, go into the game and try a wheelie.
-The WAIT. I was really expecting something good with how much the game was hyped up for a while, especially now that it's been delayed so much. If you want people to remain interested, you have to keep them up to date, at least a little information every few weeks would be cool. You can't expect people to be happy when you make them wait this long, and give them next to no information so there is no feedback from the fans until you are just about ready to launch the game.

Pixel Piracy can be resumed as a concept game with unhealthy obsessions for poop deck jokes and pixelated bleeding. The concept works simply and well enough to be fun for about 20 hours of game play, then it gets quite repetitive. You side scroll pirate ship battles, build a ship and a crew from your plunders and find booty yarr! That's about it.
For it's peculiar game play and to encourage Indie game developers I have no problem recommending it, but don't expect to find much more than what's on the cover.

This is a great game. You can be a pirate and sail through seas. Who wouldn't want to be a pirate!? Ever since I was a little boy born in the western europe I dreamt about pillaging villages and finding treasures and sinking ships. This game offers all that from the safety of my cosy chair. But wait, theres more! Pixel Piracy isn't just about violence and cruelty. It's a game about friendship. You travel through the world expieriencing new adventures each time you set sail, but you cannot do it without the help of your lovely crew you hired in a local tavern. You become friends and your bond grows stronger with every enemy you defeat.
That is of course if you pay them salary.
Otherwise they'll kill you while you sleep.

I have been so excitedly telling everyone about this game I actually forgot to properly review it.
It's a bit late now, but for the principle of it:
This is a perfect parody of dating sims - which laughs WITH fans of the genre instead of laughing AT them - used as a long-form introductory wrapping to a marvelous, intensely emotional visual novel about dreams, friendship and hope.
… with pigeons.
Although I had heard of the game since its release in English, i couldn't play it and stayd away from spoilers and forums, and I am SO glad I did! The impact of wandering the various storylines is so much more intense when you have no idea what's about to happen… The game manages to surprise & shock you almost every. single. time, despite your probable initial expectations that "a dating sim with pigeons? NOTHING will shock me any more…" JUST. YOU. WAIT.
I have the deepest respect and admiration for the author, who managed to take a lighthearted April's fools joke demo and turn it into such a well-thought, deep and engaging real story… without sacrificing any of the initial fun & WTFness. This is a masterpiece of storytelling.
And yet, when all is over and you're still reeling from the emotional rollercoaster that is the second half of the game (for best effect, play the "fulfilling a promise" path LAST, and in one single sitting!), the only way you feel you can describe the game to outsiders still seems to be : "it's a dating sim… but with pigeons. And then it gets INTENSE, and you will cry."
10/10, would cry again.
PS: Okosan is the most precious cinnamon r- err, pudding of all birdies, and deserves all the hugs.

I have the game Ship Simulator 2008, which I got in 2008. After watching youtube videos I wanted the game, but even though it looks better, it's not really.
Likes: You can deploy ships, such as lifeboats, rescue boats, zodiacs. Many more Enviroments are given, Sydney, Bora Bora, Antarctica. Great ships, airplanes, realistic sinkings. Lots of features that were in Ship Sim 2008: New Horizons are in this game like Padstow, Jumbo Javelin, etc, aswell as new features never before seen
Dislikes: In Ship simulator 2008 Mission Editor, if you wanted to pick up or drop off something like people or containers, you sail to the pick up point and they board or leave in a short time.  In Extremes it is way different. You must change the visibility of an object. E.g if a passenger you must pick up is standing on the dock, when the time comes to for the pick up, you change the visibilty to 0 and select the visibility of a passenger sitting on the ship to 1. The Mission Editor is very complicated and takes a very long time to master. In simple terms it's like saying that when you wake up in the morning you must give a very detailed description of the events that happened, such as what time did you go to bed at, did you use the bathroom, when did you first wake up, etc. The Mission Editor in Ship sim 2008 is less complicated and can be mastered after a short while.
In SSE if you're still on board when the ship sinks, regardless if this is a mission or Free roaming, you fail. In SS08 you only fail if it's a mission. In SS08 if you depart Hambourg or Rotterdam you enter an open sea enviroment. But in SSE there is only 1 open sea enviorment: The Atlantic Ocean. Meaning that if you depart Sydney for Bora Bora and then want to do something in an open sea, it has to be the Atlantic. I think that there should be the North Sea, Pacific and Atlantic Oceans in the game, instead of just the Atlantic.
This game has many great features that I like, but for people who have Ship Simulator 2008 I would highly recommend not getting this game and getting New Horizons.

I can't recommend this game at the moment, mainly due to price. The combat can be fun and it feels like a step up from warband, which could be a good thing or a bad thing.
Content at the moment comes in three flavours:
CONQUEST: Around a dozen or so battles fought over changing terrain which mainly involves capturign and holding the flag for a set amount of time. The initial round is in a team deathmatch style, with unlimited respawns. When a flag is captured the winning team must then defend it  from the other team, the only thing is, everyone only has one life so things can get dicey.
SKIRMISH: Never actually got to play a round of skirmish so far.
DUEL: Fight other players 1v1 - i'd recommend this for new players just so they can get some practice in as the real thing can make it hard to learn right away.
You gain xp from killing, assisting kills or just being in the vicinity of fighting, as well as bigger bonuses for a round ending and a "Campaign" ending. When I say "Campaign" I just mean the point when all scores are reset and teams are shuffled.
You gain levels and choose to put points into 4 different stats, so you decide whether you want to be able to swing a bit faster, take more damage, move faster etc.
Gaining xp also acts as a progress bar so you can unlock new gear to use. You start out with some padded cloth and a variety of low tier weapons to start out with. What you use is up to you. This is the main thing that kept me playing.
If it's on sale for 50% then get it, otherwise it might be worth waiting for new content.

Clever power ups and gating.  Retro but Interesting art style.  Good difficulty but mostly easy bosses.  One of the better Metro-vania games I've ever played - highly recommended for fans of the genre.

Axiom verge is a throw back to the old NES/SNES Metroid style gameplay that some call Metroidvania that references Castlevania and Metroid.  It is a side scrolling shooter that plays about as fast as Metroid or Castlevania and can easily become difficult if you increase the difficulty.
The story is based on a scientist that has something go wrong in his lab and then he ends up elsewhere.  Without going further into the story, it gets unique to say the least.  You get a multitude of different weapons, one for each number key on your keyboard and a few secrets as well as abilities that enable you to access more parts of the level. Things like phase shifting through walls to upgraded weapon power and health nodes.
The graphics on the store page are what you get.  A retro throwback to the golden days of gaming.  As you explore the level you will find secrets in the walls as well as secret levels that give you more upgrades.  Overall, my play time logged is how long it took me to finish the game with most of everything collected.  You can speed run the game in a much quicker fashion if you like but you miss out on the exploration and the bosses can be considerbly harder without additional power or health increases.
My only complaint, is without hard mode, the bosses are incredibly easy to beat and can be cheesed with ease.  Even the final boss was relativelty easy.  As I have said before, this can be remedied with hard mode and can make things a bit more difficult and possibly frusterating.
For anyone looking at a side scrolling action platformer, I would recommend this game.  I couldn't pull myself away at times and wanted to keep on playing.  When a game does that to the player, it tends to show how well designed it is.  I hope there is a sequel planned, I had read talks about it but who knows.  The story was well designed and threw a curveball at me as I progressed, which is an awesome way to immerse the player.
The only negative things I can think of with this game that would detract and possible sway a purchase is that the bosses are indeed cheesable.  Even on hard, you can still cheese them but everything else is generally much more difficult.

One of my favorite games of all time, amongst the plethora of fantastic and inventive games that have surfaced over the last 30 years, is Metroid Fusion for the GBA. It had a fantastic story, superb controls, the extensive length and repla ability associated with the Metroid series, and some of the most suspenseful and immersive music that I have ever heard from interactive media.
Axiom verge reminds me of this game in all of the best ways. It has a fantastic soundtrack, a lengthy hour count for being such a small game (took me 11 hours to complete the story mode at ~60% item collection), and visuals that match the old Metroid games perfectly. This is undoubtedly a game for the sake of nostalgia, bringing back the feel and attraction of old Metroid games while adding an entirely unique world and story. It is extremely difficult to believe that so much variety and creativity came from one developer, who managed to create what I must call a masterpiece.
That being said, there are a few issues I would point out to both the developer and to those who have an interest in playing this game:
- It is extremely challenging, but not always in the best ways: Most of the bosses and enemies are creative, unique, and require some problem solving to defeat that make each new area a pleasure to find. However, some enemies (heavy turrets and a boss you will recognize when you fight it) are simply infuriating, as their patterns make them nearly impossible to skirt or stun using even the best end-game weapons. However, a bit of patience and well-placed fleeing can mitigate this issue.
- There are so...many...guns: This game involves an  upgrade system common to the Metroid series, in which new items unlock new areas by adding some new form of movement that allows the player to access new parts of the map that they passed earlier in past areas. Included amongst these upgrades are a plethora of different weapon types that can be equipped at any time once they are found. However, there are ~30 different weapons, which means that any normal player finds 4 that they like and never use any of the others. This could be interpreted as a positive aspect of the game, adding a large selection to the player, but I prefer a smaller selection of weapons that are individually more useful. This makes the weapon selection much more akin to the tool selection from any LoZ game.
- No instruction or direction whatsoever: Again, this could be interpreted as a positive aspect of the game, forcing the player to search for their objective rather than being pointed in a particular direction and being told to fetch. However, I have found that a small amount of instruction (what you should be doing and a general idea of where to do it) is preferable to no instruction at all, simply because it removes the 1 1/2 hours devoted to backtracking to find that one door that you can open now. In an attempt to help prospective players without directly spoiling anything, I would recommend that players assume that the tools they are given are capable of doing more than what they say, and that no two tools perform exactly the same task (IE some tools may be useful for doing things other than what their explicit instruction text says in-game).
These are my main concerns with the game, but otherwise I found it extremely enjoyable and unique. I would highly recommend this game to anyone that enjoys old 8-bit metroid-vania games and unique science-fiction.

This is the game that renewed my faith in RPG Maker games. It's got that gritty steampunk shine, a good story, likeable characters and reminds me of a time when RPGs had stories that weren't convoluted with forced deep meaning and abstract elements. Skyborn tells the story of a young vagabond mechanic who steals an airship after she is sold off to marry some rich snob. Soon they are joined by a vibrant cast of characters who help them on their quest to save the world.
That about sums up the game. It seems to be just the right length and battle environments are never mindnumbingly long. Now while the majority of games like this tend to be on the long side I spent about 10 - 12 hours playing and that's because I couldn't find one of the quests. If there's anything the game could work on it's the quest system. Sure there's a quest menu and that alludes to where you go next but I got confused on where to go for one of the NPC side quest. None of this is consequential for finishing the game but I try to be as complete as possible.
The battle system was also simple enough that at the harder setting required a bit of strategy. I've still yet to conquer the bosses on hard mode yet. I fear that would require a lot of grinding to reach those levels. Overall this game was a delight to play and I definitely felt like it was money well spent and the developer put a lot of thought into this title.

This is probably one of the best RPG games made on RPGMaker that I have ever played. Another one that I enjoyed as much is Eternal Senia. The storyline, characters, graphics, and music are all charming. Best yet, you can avoid the monsters so you don't have to have endless battles (unless you want to). There's also very little grinding needed to go from one boss to the next which is great. Now, is the game worth the full cost? In my view, no. The main reason I say this is not because I don't like the game but because the game can be beat in less than 20 hours. I bought it on sale which was completely worth it.

By all means, this game deserves a negative review. It plays like silk, at a smooth 60 fps, but..that doesn't help ist much when it has less complexity than even dynasty warriors. You enter HDD and press X, or as Noire, Y, to release a wide sweeping attack. The enemies are mindless, and the gameplay is tedious, especially when objectives like "Defeat 1500" enemies appear. The clothes tearing feature is..pretty much useless, though I'd suggest getting a nude patch like I did for the jiggle physics the game has to offer.
The dialogue is generally pretty charming, if you can stand to read through all of it. Like any JRPG, it's a mountain of text upon another mountain of text. The voice acting is decent, be it English, or japanese.
You can run through the entire game in 8, boring, very wasteful hours, and the game definately isn't worth the full asking price.
..So why does this game still get a positive review from me? Hell if I know. I'm still caught in the charm like anyone else who loves the series. Sure, it was mindless, tedious work. Sure, it wasn't really all that fun..but I'll be damned if I said I wanted to stop, because for some god-only-knows reason, I didn't. Pick the game up for 7-8, and you'll be golden.

I've only played for about 100 minutes, but I can tell from half of the story missions that the game is just okay.  The gun-play is pretty bad, the parkour is lackluster, but the selection of guns is nice.  Adding to that, you're not pidgeon holed into two guns for the entire game.  You have a steady collection of pistols, SMGs, Rifles, and DMRs so you won't be having much trouble building a loadout.
My main problem with this game is the mission structure.  You're given a timer and a nebulous objective.  That objective could be defend something, it could be take something.  There's no real indication of what you should be doing because there are always multiple objectives, and the narrator and the other players/AI are always yelling out different commands.  This makes trying to get things done a little bit wonky.
The AI is also pretty godawful.  Whether you're trying to defend a point, or destroy a mobile target, your AI partners will NOT help you.  Their main objective is a death-match while your opponents will simply be to complete their objective of taking a point, defending one, or pushing a mobile target.
On a technical level, the game is kind of a mess.  Fullscreen on a non-native resolution is a joke, it doesn't run terribly well for a game made in 2011 and the animations just seem overdone.  Looking at the character customization menu, your character always looks like he's effing insane and about to go on a rampage (which would make sense if you wore the Cannibal mask).  Even on idle, the character just looks like he's trying to move every single part of his body all at the same time.  It makes judging faces and gear pieces a little bit hard.
In the end, it's a bland, rather forgettable shooter with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI and a dead playerbase.  The scenery looks great and there are a lot of fun guns, but that's all this game really has going for it.  It's free-to-play so pick it up if you want, but you're not going to be blown away.  It's just whelming.  Not overwhelming, or underwhelming.  It's just alright.

This is one of those games that made me wish there was more than just a "Yes" or "No" button on Steam. Brink is a meh. It's the worst thing Brink could have been. Meh.
Let's start with the things Brink get's right, and it get's a good few things right:
There's lots of customisation to your characters, and while most of it is locked away, I can at least feel some sort of individuality.
The voice acting is pretty good, and the story from what I've seen is interesting, though constricted to cut scenes only.
The game looks nice, and while the graphics are dated now a little, Brink is a unique looker. Imagine Borderlands if it didn't look terrible and was actually inspired. It's really cool.
Alright, those are the things about Brink that are good. Let's get to the meh.
There are lots of guns in Brink, though every SMG is basically the same, there's like 3 different ARs really. The weapon selection is interesting but it could be cooler. There's nothing in Brink that blows my socks off except a Full Auto Grenade Launcer.
Speaking of weapons, the shooting in the game isn't very good. It's not bad, it could be worse, but it's pretty bland.
There are 3 different character sizes, Light, Medium, and Heavy. This is cool, and there are genuine hand-offs to being one size over the other. The problem is that they aren't all unlocked from the start when they really should be. This is a big trend in Brink.
The Freedom of movement in Brink is kind of cool, but is hampered by the fact that not many maps in Brink take advantage of it. The maps are pretty, but they were designed like the player isn't a parkour machine. Though, the parkour kind of feels bad, the camera is really awkward when climbing.
Alright, let's get to the things that are bad.
There are four classes in Brink, which is cool, and the classes are well balanced between each other some what. Here's the problem though, the level up system is really bad for the classes. The upgrades you can get only do good things, which means a person who has played the game more will be objectivly better/more useful than someone who has played the game less. An Engineer who can place heavy turrets is way better than an Engineer that can only place light turrets, or even worse, no turrets.
Here's an even bigger issue. There are upgrades that are universal, that have some really good stuff that have no trade-offs. Stuff like reloading while sprinting, extra health, making no noise while running, being able to see the direction of someone aiming at you, and being able to shoot people while downed. These abilities are objectivly good, there's no reason to not have them. It really destroys the balance between new players and old ones.
The game is unbalanced on a map per map basis. Basically, whoever is defending is probably going to win. Both sides have the exact same tools at their disposal, and considering that being able to place turrets is a thing, defenders almost always win. I've played about 9 matches, every single one where we were defending, our team won, and everyone where we were attacking we lost. Also, objective variety is pretty weak, you pretty much do the same thing everytime with slight differences. Nothing to write home about.
There is some stuttering issues at times that is kind of weird. Even worse, if you want to play single-player, you're going to have to deal with a 30-FPS lock, which is like driving brake pads into your eyes after playing 60 FPS multiplayer.
Team communication has no aids. You can't place markers, you can't tell who is going to what objective. It's all typing and voice coms, and it's really bad.
In conclusion, it's pretty easy to see why Brink did poorly when it came out, even though it had an impressivly large advertising campaign behind it. It's not a bad game per se, mostly now that the game it's free, but the problem with the game lies with the fact that the game it's clunky and messy in the vast majority of things, the shooting feels heavy, controlling your character feels as if you're moving a tank, while this type of "feel" would work in some games, in Brink that is specifically a game that it's trying to incentivize movility and agility this doesn't work nearly as well, half of the times it feels frustrating and tedious to simply move around the map, pair that up with the fact that the pc version of this game, while being the vest of the three available ones, it's not really a good pc version at that, the game supports high resolutions (1080p, don't know if more, sorry) and the textures are detailed, that's good, as well as the overall aesthetic, it's unique.
The bad it's that the game it's deserted online, and with the campaign being essentially multiplayer but with cutscenes, and bots, locked at 30 framerates per second with no known workaround, there really isn't that much to love about the game.
It's not even worth to enter into the whole "debate" about whether 30 fps is playable or not, that it's entirely relative as it is subjective, the problem here it's that essentially we have a game that can run at 60 framerates per second, and yet for one reason or another it can't unless you're playing online.
The graphics menu it's also incredibly vague, with only having a couple of options, nothing really crucial it's missing but it would have been better to have more.
The biggest problem with Brink, NOW, years after it's release, it's that there are so many alternatives to this game, and the game in itself, even by going free to play, will, in my opinion, not attract that many people if not for the first days of this new practice.
People didn't buy Brink because of it's price, people didn't buy Brink because there really isn't that many reasons to buy it, the game was supposed to be a brink (no pun intended) of innovation (whatever that word means) paired with the attempt of the game trying to create it's own individuality, instead we got a clunky game that tried to replicate mechanics from other bigger and more popular shooters, but that fails miserably in introducing any of it's own, besides the cool aesthetic and concept there really isn't anything here to keep an eye out.
There are just so many different alternatives that are so much better than this, mostly when it comes to pc, there are, if not then, then now, literally thousands of games that can offer much more than what Brink does.
If only maybe they patched the 30 fps, then maybe I could recommend it on the merit alone that you can dress your character with some cool costumes and maybe imagine for a second that you're playing as some kind of villain, creating your own stories as you play this hollow and mediocre game... The game is a pretty decent HOI game by itself. You choose a country, and lead it in the years leading up to the Second World War. There are many, many fun or interesting mods for this game, available to download on the Steam Workshop, ranging from alternative history mods exploring what would happen had the Germans won WWI, to mods taking place in different times, such as WWI or today, from overall balance mods to some really wacky crazy things like what if the world was upside down. There really is something out there for everyone.

I wouldn't have recommended this game on launch as it had a number of MAJOR issues. A year and a half later, it is up to a consistently playable level and most of the time is genuinely fun. There are still some major areas for improvement (notably naval combat) but Paradox have shown a willingness to continue fixing things. The DLCs are a bit of a mixed bag, I feal that Death or Dishonor was worth the asking price while the main thing I found beneficial in Together for Victory was the Blitz order (which really should be in the base game, in my opinion). The upcoming DLC (Waking the Tiger) looks to have a lot of interesting and useful features. Time will tell if it meets expectations.
CAUTIONARY NOTE: Paradox across the board has developed a bad habit of continually changing games so that you are practically forced to buy DLC in order to have a properly balanced game. I dislike this practice but don't feel like it reflects overly negatively on Hearts of Iron 4 at this time to warrant a downvote (omission of the Blitz order notwithstanding). I would be very cautious of Europa Universalis 4 or Crusader Kings 2 if you only intend to buy the base game.
TL;DR: It's a good game that has some minor issues. The devs are still regularly putting out patches and updates though so it will probably get better as we move forward.

I really want to recommend this game but in its current state I just can't. While I loved the concept and the gameplay, the dealbreaker for me was the bugs. They tried my patience until I finally just got tired of playing.
Though I encountered several bugs, the one that was extremely frequent, irritating, and ultimately made me quit playing was when you order your crew or captain to disembark onto an island they frequently get stuck near the edge of the island. When this happens to your captain, you cannot progress, forcing you to reload the game to the last save. When it happens to your crew members (sometimes multiple crewman at a time) the only way I found I could get them unstuck was to issue an order to send them back to the ship...at which point they promptly dove into the ocean and drowned (unless they had the swimming perk). Thus, you are forced to either reload the last save or accept the loss of crew members you may have spent a long time leveling up and upgrading.
If this happened occasionally I could have overlooked it, but I was finding myself reloading my game and replaying the same island encounter over and over again until I just happened to be lucky enough not to have any of my crew get stuck. Then I would go to another island and start the process all over again.
Bottom line, I really enjoyed the game when I wasn't dealing with bugs, but the bugs just became too much of a burden and caused more frustration than the game is worth.

Yeah, this may not have a great story like Bioshock and neither spectacular graphics like Crysis. But I'm sure as hell that you'll find it amazing if you just try it out. This game is like Bomberman and Subway Surfers had babies. It even has a nice old-school arcade touch on it. The goal of the game is to survive as long as you can, while blasting enemies and destroying enemy bases in order to get a better high score. I don't really know why people don't like this game, I really love it, it's exactly my type of game! If you've used to waste at least 2 hours per day playing Atomic Bomberman with your family like me, then you'll have a lot of nostalgia and fun moments with this game. You can even play it with your kid because of the simplistic and beautiful graphics it has, and both of you will get some fun out of playing it.
- A lot of mission objectives to let you entertained.
- The game is still getting updated. The developers even added achievements and trading cards after a few requests of them. They are also thinking of implementing multiplayer in their game.
- The music changes accordingly to the map you're in. And let me tell you that the rock music fits the game perfectly, it keeps you motivated.
- You can proceed in different zones by destroying enough enemy bases. Right now, there are 4 themes for them. The forest, the desert, the christmas and one I didn't have the luck to find yet.
- The mazes are procedurally generated, so you can go around the world as many times as you would like, there will always be a new maze and new enemies waiting for you.
- The Tornado power is badass as hell!
- You can upgrade the powers you receive.
- You have the opportunity of upgrading your powers even more after you've leveled up a few times.
- It's a very relaxing and simple game which keeps your mind away from real life problems.
- The sound won't keep hearing if you've Alt+Tabbed the game. This is a big plus for some guys!
- The settings page has options for: Quality Level, Screen Resolution, Windowed Mode, V-sync, Anti Alias, Music Volume and Sound Volume.
- Friendly graphics for all the ages.
- Collect coins and use them to customize your game, BomberZone includes 5 different soldier types and 16 different types of bombs to choose from.
-  7 different power-ups to help you in your quest of torturing those aliens.
- The UI screen looks like a mobile game, which is not entirely bad, but it feels a bit weird on PC.
- I've searched a while for the Leaderboards page but I can't seem to find it.
- It lacks multiplayer, which would have made this game a lot funnier than it already is.
- Still needs a bit of polishing. I've encountered a few bugs while playing it. Bugs like:
1. There was a time when I've detonated a bomb but the bomb was still showing up on the screen and I could just pass throught it like I was a ghost.
2. At random times, the game will tell me I've come to a new region even though I was still on the same map.
3. If you die exactly when you've received the Tornado power, you will continue to respawn spinning infinitely, one funny bug till you learn you'll have to exit and re-enter the game for it to fix up.
If Bomberman games are something you've spend much hours of your life on, I would gladly recommend you to try this game right on. It has the fully potential of being a next big clone of Bomberman, only a bit different. I hope that the developers will keep updating this game with new stuff. A new multiplayer mode will surely attract a lot of new people in the game. And heck, it will become the new addiction in our life.

The cake might be a lie, but the inventiveness and enjoyable gameplay of Portal sure isn't. Portal is all about platforming puzzles and I usually hate those parts in games like Darksiders, because they're too damn restrictive/linear. You either do things *exactly* like the developers want you to, at the *exact* spots where you're allowed to do it or you die and restart at the latest checkpoint.
Not only does Portal feature manual saving anywhere, it doesn't feel like you're doing the gaming equivalent of following an instruction manual. I haven't explored how many ways there are to solve each puzzle, but the game lets you play around and see what works for you, which feels great. There are some places where can't place portals as well as puzzles where you have to target a small area to succeed, but most of the time it felt like I could choose what suited me best.
Falling through a portal is quite exhilarating and some puzzles require you to place a portal directly beneath you before you land, extending that rush and making it feel like you're flying, bending physics to your will. There is no fall damage if you miss a jump, even if there are other ways you can die. It can sometimes be hard to quickly enough get your bearings when falling through a portal, but I didn't have much problem with that. It also didn't bother me that there mostly wasn't any background music, just the sound of moving machine parts or not even that (no surprise given how Valve makes their games). You hear from the AI Glados regularly, though, and she/it is fun to listen to.
As others have pointed out, this game is quite short, but the end still dragged on a bit more than I would have liked. At least, the final boss fight wasn't that hard or tedious.

Overall, Skyborn is a lot of fun to play and well worth the money.
The effect of the early Final Fantasy games on the RPG genre is immense. That influence is felt very clearly in Skyborn. You can tell the makers of this game were inspired by Final Fantasy VI in particular. While some of the characters feel like they were lifted right out of FFVI, it's nowhere close to how World Heroes cloned Street Fighter.
It lacks a clear writing style. The writing is strangly good at times and completely empty at others. It's almost like they were attempting to use different language patterns for the different characters (which would be great) but sometimes confused themselves with regards to who is speaking during the scripted events.
The combat system is a wonderful reformulation of the standard turn-based systems with which any RPG player would be familiar. Yet, the one way Skyborn sets itself apart from other RPGs is in how it eschews constant combat by providing glowing experience "crystals" throughout the maps. These keep the story line moving forward, keeping the player on track for the next challenges without having to dedicate time specifically to leveling up characters. The drive to find these cheap experience locations also encourages exploration, which gives the player a chance to lose themself in the charming SNES-era graphics, complete with parallax scrolling effects to bring out the stratified society story line.
If you ever enjoyed an SNES RPG, especially a Final Fantasy installment, you'll probably like this game.

Forbidden platitudes in this review: Metroidvania, Nintendo, love letter, retro, Super Metroid, indie, pixel art, 90's, 8-bit, chiptune, nostalgia.
is deeply rooted in the 2D action/platform adventure genre. Aside from excelling in every area, what sets it apart is a compelling intrigue and a wide range of pretty unique mechanisms, which I will do my best not to spoil here.
The first right note that the game hits is the atmosphere. The visual design might not be everyone's cup of tea (it surely wasn't mine at first), but the somewhat crude colours of this alien world in which you find yourself stranded play their part in creating a deep sense of immersion. The sounds and music are on point, and set the perfect mood for the 12-15 hours you'll probably spend exploring and backtracking across the different areas on a casual playthrough.
The sense of progression is extremely satisfying throughout the adventure. The level design teases you along the way with a good number of inaccessible areas and/or pickups, which you'll be encouraged to revisit once you've acquired new tech. Aside from lore logs and the usual upgrades (health, range, weapon damage), a good number of the items you will find are inherently specific to
and will have unique consequences on the gameplay. The movement upgrades really redefine the platforming, and the rather sizeable pool of weapons will leave you with a lot of options when it comes to combat.
The difficulty balance was just right for me - some of the end-game rooms and bosses are pretty brutal, but exploring and acquiring enough upgrades will make it possible to push through without too much grinding and frustration. With a clear mind and a bit of experience with the genre, finding your way on your own is perfectly possible (and I would deeply recommend doing so, as it is infinitely more satisfying than following a guide). The more hardcore-oriented players will be glad to know about the inclusion of a Hard mode as well as a built-in Speedrun mode, complete with global/split timers, reduced RNG and leaderboards with separate categories (any%, 100%, low%)! Nonetheless,
is perfectly suited for casual gameplay as well.
Did I mention one person did all of this? Yep. The coding, the art, the level design, the music (!)... all the work of a single man, Tom Happ, who created
as a personal project in his spare time over the course of five years. For a game this close to perfection in every area and a product far above the industry's usual finishing standards, this is truly impressive.

The one thing I'll criticize here is the lack of direction the game provides you with.  Even in exploration based games like Castlevania or Legend of Zelda, there are usually SOME hints of where to go and what to do.  I have spent hours searching for my next objective.  Some areas are difficult to traverse, and so it gets frustrating when I can't figure out where I should be!  Note that I enjoy explorative games.  I don't enjoy being forced to backtrack repeatedly until I can miraculously find the new area the power up I found an hour ago opens for me.
Overall, still a fun game.  I'm almost finished with it (last boss), so I'll update again soon.

Well, I am a Neptunia fanboy, I saw this spin-off and decided to give it a try.  And beside all those "Nep-Nep is in" kind of useless review, I am going to give my two cents on this game.
First, the disappointments.  It is similar to some Japanese-style hack-slash games such as Dynasty Warrior from Koei, among them Orochi Warrior Z is my all time favourite game.  Unfortunately this games pales too much in comparism to Koei's flagship series.
1. The battle field (or dungeon) size, are you even serious? You have access to all the dungeons from Neptunia and you decide only to utilise like less than 1% of the area of each dungeon?
2. The battle field, just too simple too plain.  In Warrior series you have friends cheering and enemies cursing you on battle field,  and there are tactics you should follow, be it diversion, infiltration or direct confrontation.  Sadly, in this game, you are all alone, there is nobody accompany you.
3. The weapon system, the skill system, all absent.  The characters are just about levels, nothing more.
As I was thinking for a refund, I found this game is not all bad.  It is strangely addicting.  I would try to give a few reason for this,
1. It is simple, yet not braindead.  As I thought this game is going to be too easy, I was killed serveral times during the 3rd mission.  Blindly go into the stack of monsters and mash buttons at your own peril.
2. Again, it is simple.  No need to google or wikia for whatever hidden artefacts, or secret mission, or true ending.  No need to worry if you missed some sythesis materials. And, no need to grind.  If you feel tired or bored, play a few round of this game feels relaxing.
3. Some design is very interesting.  There are missions (or dungeon) where the objective is hidden so you need to figure things out. There are also dungeons where monsters are strong but objective is simple, so the usual "kill-everything-that-moves" mentality for hack&slash games can get you into serious trouble.
4. Character skills, attacks and HDD are well designed.  Many attacks of character also has certain property.  Such as Vert's weak attack ending is able to paralyse your foe.  It can be a game changer.  Uni's weak attack is ridiculously bad,  but in HDD, her attack do wonders. Nepgear's HDD weak attack is god like... There are just too much stuff to explore. So again, simple at the same time not brain dead.
5. Actually I would like the main series to use this style instead of the battle followed by encoutering the monster.  It is much more engaging and faster-paced.  If not, I would like to see if they are willing to improve this spin-off and add more features, to make the game on par with the Wariror series,  then this game can be very good, even surpass the main series.
So, verdict?
If you're look for a good hack-slash game, run away from this game, the price tells you all.  As someone said, there are much better ones out there.
If you're a Neptunia fanboy like me, or like relaxing anime games in general,  this is quite a good pick, especially on sale.

I picked up Hell Yeah! as something Halloweeny to play last fall and I was worried I made a bad call, but it has enough blood and hellfire to count, I think. You play Ash, the skeletal bunny prince of Hell. Your dad croaked and some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ demon took scandalous photos of you so your mandate to rule is in question. The story is dumb and the humor errs on the side of trying too hard, but it's a good enough setup for murdering tons of demons. Which is your goal, killing 100 demons in all kinds of gruesome ways. Your main weapon is a sawblade (they call it a jetpack and I have no idea why) that lets you kill normal enemies by touching them and wear down the big named monsters. Once you wear them down you get a little WarioWare-style minigame to finish them off in some bloody, goofy way.
The platforming is solid, though the emphasis seems more on exploring to find money and secrets for upgrades than on fighting. Combat really is mostly a non-issue since you kill things by touching them and you have a ridiculous amount of health. It's colorful and cute and a little gross and has a ton to unlock, so it's not bad if you want a light platformer with some goofy style.

Hell Yeah! is an action-puzzle game that's more designed towards humor and is never too difficult. The game is at least mediocre when you have weapons, and terribly boring when you don't. On the other hand, the boss kill animations are great (even if there are too few unique ones). I highly recommend playing it with a controller.

I had originally planned to get this game shortly after it's initial release back in 2010, but after hearing news that Episode 1 ended on a cliffhanger and the publisher (Atari) was holding back the release of Episode 2, I decided against it.
However, now that Atari's license/publishing rights to the game has expired, Blade Kitten is back on track in the hands of the developer, Episode 2 is in development, and Episode 1 is better than ever with full Xbox 360 Controller support, an option to unlock the framerate from 30 to 60fps, and support for higher resolutions. Oh, and did I mention that the price has been reduced to roughly 1/3 of its original cost with Episode 2 planned to be released at around the same price?
Gameplay-wise, Blade Kitten is a solid 2D Action Platformer with tight controls, good physics, decent combat, fun level design, and enough optional exploration/collectibles to appeal to folks who are into that sort of thing.
Graphics-wise, Blade Kitten looks good. The graphics are by no means ground-breaking or cutting-edge, (this is a game from 2010 by a rather small developer, after all) but they serve their purpose by illustrating a colorful and interesting world.
Sound-wise, the game is average but adequate. The voice acting is decent and the music (while somewhat forgettable) is by no means unpleasant to listen to.
Story-wise, Blade Kitten is fun and interesting. Kit is an amusing and likeable protagonist, and most of the other characters are amusing and likeable as well. The story so far is incomplete as Episode 1 ends on a cliffhanger, but it left me wanting more and I eagerly await the release of Episode 2.
Overall, Blade Kitten is a solid buy for the price. It's a fun game that will keep fans of the genre entertained and leave them wanting more. If you enjoy 2D Action Platformers with solid gameplay, colorful graphics, and an amusing cast of characters, then I highly recommend checking out Blade Kitten.

Vacant – это короткая приключенческая игра на основе  одноименного сетевого графического романа за авторством Хитер Наннелли, которая же является и разработчиком данной игры.
Хитер Наннелли –
, но новичок в сфере разработки видео-игр.
1.
Действие в игре происходит либо в альтернативной вселенной, либо в далеком будущем, где люди живут в одном городе с представителями иных человекообразных видов. Главная героиня - стажер в правительственном агентстве «Око» и в первый же день ее назначили на дело о трех пропавших гражданах.
Мир игры мог бы быть интересным, если бы Хитер привнесла в игру больше информации из своего графического романа.
К сожалению, сама история, которая так многообещающе началась, закончилась ничем. Не раскрыты ни характеры персонажей, ни их мотивация (особенно это касается странного инопланетянина). Вот такие картонные персонажи без настоящих эмоций. Почему никто не проявляет никаких эмоций на грубость, угрозу убийства или появление призраков?
Из-за своей продолжительности (менее 1 часа) и нелепого сюжета игра Хитер Наннелли больше напоминает демо-версию, а не законченную игру.
2.
В игре от вас требуется только ходить, разговаривать и читать/смотреть на активные объекты. Вам не придется напрягать мозг, решая пазлы или отыскивая секреты и предметы, потому что эта игра является симулятором ходьбы.
В игре существуют серьезные проблемы с этим самым хождением: главная героиня двигается очень медленно и периодически застревает.
3.
При разговоре/ рассматривании предметов можно выбрать вариант реплики/ действия, но ваш выбор ни на что не влияет. Кроме того, в текстах есть опечатки и ошибки.
4.
Портреты персонажей, появляющиеся при разговорах, хорошего качества и написаны в интересном стиле. Именно из-за этих портретов и тега в Стиме «приключенческая игра» я и решил купить игру. К моему разочарованию в самой игре качество 3-Д моделей явно хуже портретов. Игра не идет в полноэкранном режиме, а разработчица игры не может решить эту проблему.
5.
Звуки в игре стандартно-бесплатные, а
в игре не слышна. В рекламном ролике вы можете услышать Холли Стэндбрук в качестве рассказчика.
6.
Игра продолжительностью меньше одного часа, с картонными персонажами и скучной историей, не стоит того, чтобы ее покупать.

is a point&click adventure but not in a traditional sense. There are no items or puzzles to solve. I think it has more in common with walking simulators that focus on story delivery and aesthetics (and I will criticise it only on those elements) Usually games in the point&click genre are either 2D or 3D so I do like the use of an isometric camera. The game looked a lot better in a trailer but I soon realized that it looks a lot less appealing once you get to control it. I generally like the aesthetic of this game although there is no fullscreen and the world in general has low detail. Ultimately I found individual parts of the game not complementing each other and it was a underwhelming experience even for the low price.
The story takes place in some kind of society where humans live and breed with other species.  Our character moves to a new place and is hired by mysterious organization. I guess you could call it a crime narrative with a supernatural fantasy twist. I think they were going for a big plot twist but the narrative was handled poorly. There are many confusing plot points so I am not really sure what happened. You get many text choices throughout the game although I don't think they change much ( there is a way to get extended ending based on one important action )
Probably the biggest problem is the lack of genuine reaction from the main character. She does not comment on anything disturbing that would make me crap my pants in real life. Like I want to know what character is thinking right now. This game should have a lot of tension in regards to the story but Jade(us) is reacting casually or not at all. (she takes it like a robot)
Music did not add anything to the atmosphere and I found the soundtrack borderline irritating. I love ambient music but all I hear is one note vibration. There are moments when you should feel some tension when you are in danger. However, the music in this game almost never matches the tone of the situation. There was some decent voice acting in the trailer and almost none of it was in the game. In fact, some of the voice acting that was meant to be creepy felt really out of place. Also, I think this game would have benefited from having more sound effects.
Last but not least, the game has some glitches and pathing problems. Which I could tolerate if the story was better. In this case, the controlling problems were the final nail in the coffin that soaked out little fun I had. I beat it in 40 minutes and had no satisfaction.
The combination of poor design, confusing plot points, and subpar pathing made it a rather poor experience. I don't know much about the material on which this game is based but I hope it was a poor adaptation. I think a plot in this game could work if the story was more coherent. Each element of this game is average at best and the story did not have a consistent flow to it. It is a pretty cheap game but it kind of matches the quality.

If you're into point-and-click adventures then Vacant may be up your alley.  It doesn't really offer anything groundbreaking or amazing, but it's fun for what it is and comes at a relatively cheap price.  The story is probably the biggest draw and, if you're anything like me, will get pulled in and want to know what happens next.  I'm also a sucker for murder mystery type stuff.
I will say there are a number of issues I do have with the game.  It's sluggish - your character moves at a snails pace and I really wish something like double-clicking would make her run to her location.  The act of moving itself is sometimes a chore as the pathing is awkward at times, requiring you to go much further around something than you should need to.  There are some spelling errors along the way, too, but nothing too terrible.  These are all relatively minor issues that hopefully the developer will tighten up in any possible updates.
Again, I don't expect Vacant to really blow anyone away, but it's definitely good enough and I don't really have any issues with recommending it to people.

Pixel Piracy is a 2D side-scrolling adventure game developed by Quadro Delta. The game puts you in the shoes of a pirate captain with a mission to defeat four legendary pirates. During your quest you'll have to recruit crew members, train them, arm them, fight rival pirates and imperial ships, loot said ships or capture them if you so desire. If that sounds like fun to you, then let the disappointment commence! Pixel Piracy is a disaster.
The game starts you off on an island, where you'll give your captain a name, change a few minor looks (face, hair, clothing color) and answer a few questions that will change a few parameters of your gameplay (more ship encounters, less encounters, more starting gold, higher loot rates...etc) and you're off and running. In the beginning you'll be tasked to hire crew members, design your ship and set sail for treasure, knowledge, death and bordem.
The map is broken up into nodes (squares). Each node holds either an island (hostile or friendly), towns of various sizes, or ship encounters (pirate or imperial vessels). A number is given before sailing to the next node that indicates the difficulty of what you'll encounter and to help you gauge what you can handle. The combat itself is nothing to write home about; it consists of boarding a ship and letting your crew kill the opposition. Typically, it's over in a matter of seconds and requires only a few mouse clicks per battle. As you fight higher difficulty crews, you'll be able to acquire ship cannons, new weapons, and passive bonuses to help your crew survive. You'll also obtain hull components that you can use to customize your ship.
Along with better equipment, you must sustain your crew's morale, and hunger levels. Morale is effected by the cleanliness of your ship and by paying your crew their salary in gold, which is typically found from plundering ships and raiding islands. The game does have permadeath for both crew and captain. You can die from drowning, being killed in action, a wild animal, starvation or mutiny (low morale). That's about all there is to the game. It seems like a lot, but it's not very in depth.
What Pixel Piracy does right, it does a dozen more things wrong. Let's break the down game on what it did right and what it did wrong.
I felt the ship building was done well. It was easy to mix and match pieces, shuffle them around and make the ship however I wanted. Where it went wrong was with mast/sail building, which is finicky at best and broken at worst. I was forced to capture a ship with a flag/sail just to get the achievement since it wouldn't let me build my own (even with all the components).
Equiping and changing around your pirate's gear and bonuses is was well done. It was easy to move around them, switch out weapons and see what would serve me better than what I already had; a DPS counter was on all the weapons, which made it easy to pick through. However, the combat was dull and forgettable. Sure, I could and did deck out everyone in great gear, but watching them fight was boring; it was a cluster of pixelated people flying left and right, shooting here and stabbing there. There was nothing to do mid fight aside from tossing a few bandages for health. You were left as a spectator in your own game.
Several aspects: two minor ones and one major, were the most off-putting during my experiences playing. The minor aspects included the voices/sound effects and the game's weird fascination with defecation and applying that to every aspect of the game: there were achievements for your crew soiling your ship, for seagulls soiling your ship, skills to lessen said soiling of said ship and so on and so forth. It was rather absurd. With that being said, the sound effects. The voices were agitating. Between the bad singing in the taverns, my crew constantly saying random, nonsensical things and my captain sounding like she was being sexually gratified every time she said "Yes!" I couldn't tell what I hated more.
The major issue was path finding. When sailing to an island, your crew will use a grapple hook to climb down towards the island. On occasion and alarmingly frequently, they would fail to grapple either to the island or back to the ship. When that happens, the crew member would walk right into the water and drown, or jump into the air and then fall back down, also in the water and also drowning. You'd lose your crew member (remember, permadeath?) and all their gear, skills and work you put into them. To remedy this, you would have to re-load, or continue on without him/her and suffer the loss. This has been an issue for some time and the developers were made aware of it, but the problem was never resolved.


Overall, Pixel Piracy sounds good on paper, but it fails in execution. It's heavy-handed UI and AI are both cumbersome and obnoxious. It suffers from game breaking glitches that will force you to re-load the game on several occasions, or start over completely. That is, unless you don't just quit first. Pixel Piracy needs work and a lot of it at that. I tried to find a silver lining in this game. I really did; there just is no justification for something that feels so unfinished. If you're looking for a pirate themed game, look somewhere else. Pixel Piracy isn't worth the price tag or your time.

This was all around a great game. It's right down the alley for old fans of the series and new people who saw it pop up in their recommended list.
Unlike the previous turn-based combat of the rest of the franchise to this date, Neptunia U takes the hack n' slash route of RPGs. Combat in Neptunia U is extremely satisfying for a few hours, but then kind of loses its novelty after that period of time. Eventually you find a broken combo on a broken CPU, say Blanc, and spam her X+X+X+X+Y+Y combo which absolutely destroys and nothing really happens, not to mention the CPUs and Candidates are nowhere close to being equal in strength, and here's a breakdown of their power.
1. Neptune: She's the original MC of the series. Her X combo whilst in HDD does this insane AOE spin attack that destroys, whilst her non HDD form is simply forward directional attacks. Nothing special.
2. Noire: One of my favorite characters, she is surprisingly less powerful than I expected. Whilst she can go toe to toe against most enemies, her Y, which is her few AOE wave clear attacks takes a while to set up, making her damage output less that some other characters'.
3. Blanc: Some people hate on Blanc for having slow attacks, but on the contrary, her mobility combo in HDD of X+X+X+X+Y+Y makes her near untouchable and can deal 4000+ damage a hit at level 35. Blanc, at that point, is absolutely broken.
4. Vert: One of the most OP characters, her Y combos in the middle of her X combos allows her to dash from place to place, making Vert unhittable.
5. Nepgear: Her skill set is quite the same as Neptune's in HDD, but in her regular form, her X combo can extend a Y at the end which functions as a dash, much like Vert.
6. Uni, AKA Skillshot God: Why is Uni called this? Well, all her attacks are very directional. Her Ys are, most of her Xs are, and in HDD, every single attack points at the first direction the first attack goes, especially in her X combo, allowing you to move and kite every single enemy, point the gun at them, and spam. Her Y is also broken AF but takes an insane amount of time to charge up, rendering it useless when she's crowded.
7. Rom and Ram, AKA Spam Gods: I'm lumping them together due to their similar movesets. Most of their Xs in HDDs are directional, and the Ys are basically spam damage-all-enemies-in-a-huge-cone type attacks.
8. Dengekiko and Famitsu: Wow, are these 2 journalists underpowered. I mean, I swear nobody uses them unless they have to. Their basics are weak, they have no mobility or surround AOE except for Dengekiko's Ys in combo with Xs or out.
And of course, every Neptunia game has some broken item. In Neptunia 1, it was probably the Stamina Band that gave you 5000 extra health, in Neptunia 2 it was the FREE Gehaburn for Nepgear that let you one-shot every monster for at least 30 levels. In this game, it's that Scrambler Drive that allows you to, get this, instantly HDD at the beginning of every game. Couple that with the HDD gained from Costume Break, It essentially allows for each character you bring in to use their BROKEN AF EXE Drive twice. Wow.
For all of you long-time fans out there, you all know that Neptunia is a story-centered game. This game is chock full of the standard Neptunia humor. For all of you noobs out there, that includes the boob jokes,
, classic 4th wall breaks, which Idea Factory did a great job with, and the general personality of your favorite characters. However, the story is stretched a bit thin. The "Quests" in the game are the same thing, with "Irregular Quests" being the same thing but with special rules! Wow, originality. Not to mention that the story will only progress with the completion of these Irregular Quests. I was not nearly as engaged by the story in U than by the turn-based combat games, but after all, it's probably harder to time random dialogue sequences in the middle of an X combo, right?
Even if the story is not as good as the previous ones, It is still good enough to keep me playing, and the humor makes it funny as well.
This section will include graphics, sound, all that stuff.
Graphics:
Much like the rest of the games, the graphics are eh, good enough. The textures have been ripped straight from the other games and so were the enemies. Just look at the Rival Mech and Herobo from Neptunia 1, etc.
Sound:
Though Idea Factory takes a lot of songs from the first games, like $100 and Nepgear's theme, I don't care, because those songs are great. The opening song is also what I've come to expect from these games, and Idea Factory once again delivers.
Optimization and Hardware for all of you PC Nerds:
I run an Nvidia GTX 970, and it works like a charm. 300+ FPS at the most lag-inducing times, and from what I've seen, it has worked on the equivalent of a mac. Good for Idea Factory, making their games playable.
In Summary: Whether you're a new person to the series, or a hardcore Neptunia fan who's in it for another game, like the rest coming out this summer (Victory II I'm looking at you), these Neps you're getting from this Nep is well worth the Neps spent on this Nep.

Axiom Verge is just what the doctor ordered; Fun, meaty scifi metroidvania. Gameplay is responsive and smooth and there are a lot of guns in the game. None of the guns are mandatory for different bosses etc. so instead of giving you new guns that makes the old ones obsolete as you progress, it gives you a lot of options to find your own playstyle.
In the vein of old classics like Super Metroid, you explore a big map divided into several pieces. The game doesn't always tell you explicitly where to go so you're gonna have to do some exploring which is rewarding because you find different upgrades all over the maps.
Driving the events of the game is a fascinating scifi story that takes some twists and turns just when you thought that you figured it all out. It left me wanting for more of this universe and it's characters.
Music is very on point with 8-bit melodies mixed with cavernous, reverby bass drums with a little bit of glitch sounds sprinkled in to create a suitable, catchy alien aural landscape.
The visuals pay homage to the games of old with 8-bit looking -yet- high resolution sprites. The bosses especially look impressive. Whereas Super Metroid took Samus to some really claustrophobic places, Axiom Verge's visuals have a more monolithic quality to them with big, cavernous rooms with giant ancient structures hanging around in the background. Combined with some of the more ambient tracks of the game, it makes for a very effective atmosphere.
Thomas Happ has created a game that feels nostalgic yet modern and new, dressed it up with great level design and pacing, making it one of the best games of it's genre.
Highly recommended.

Decent Gameplay,  VERY Lackluster story.
This is one of those moments when steam's requirement to recommend a game or not grates on me, because this is a good enough game, but it's not great, and I certainly wouldn't recommend it to everyone. I guess, since I do recommend it to some people, that's a yes.
For the most part, this game has solid gameplay. The fun and aesthetic of metroid are captured well, and the game has enough hidden treasure and a harsh enough difficulty curve to make 100% completion worth striving for. However, if you want an interesting, compelling, or even intelligible story, I suggest looking somewhere else. The characters are poorly constructed and have personality traits that contradict their actions. Why is it that Trace has no qualms about slaughtering mutants with a flame thrower, but once he's facing a mass murdering psychopath, he suddenly gets gun shy? The whole world is very confusing and the fact that all the characters are hiding things and keeping secrets gives the game a very "I could tell you, but I won't" vibe.
As I said, though, the mechanics are mostly good. Mostly. The main problem with the gameplay is that it is possible to get stuck in area that you are underleveled for. I got trapped in one and had to turn on cheats to stand a chance in it. For the most part this shouldn't be too much of a problem, because it's usually necessary to pick up upgrades or equipment from one area of the game in order to progress, but it can still be an issue.
This gameplay issue actually exacerbates problems with the story, because the story is already convoluted and all over the place, and is very unclear about its chronology, and the fact that getting to certain areas early can allow you to watch cutscenes out of order makes it even more confusing.
Overall, get it if it's on sale, if you really like metroid, or want a challenging game without much need for story.

It combines elements of Mega Man, Castlevania Symphony of the Night and Super Metroid into a mentally ♥♥♥♥♥♥ic experience that I have not fealt in a long time.   This game brings everything to the table that the 80's babies grew up with in terms of gaming.  The controls are tight and intuitive, the weapons and tools are unique and diverse.  You will use everything the game gives you to beat it.  The boss battles are fun and turn into bullet hell battles as you damage the enemy.  Each boss has it's own unique fight involved in beating it and that point brings me to this point.  The game gives you just enough to know how to play but the game itself teaches you how it wants to be played just by playing.  This is something that gaming has been missing all to often lately.  Most games now a days hold your hand with tutorials explainig every single aspect or you get railroaded into a graphic novel with way to deviate and explore.  This game is all about exploring and backtracking.  If you have played many a metroidvania game this will be complete second nature to you.  The assets are clean and retro harkening back to Metroid on the NES, yet are unique to themselves.  The game gives a constant feeling of being alone in an alien atmosphere with the constant feeling of danger.  The enemies will mess your face up if you don't pay attention and employ some fancy footwork.  This game is such an original in the sense of story and music.  Oh the music!  The tracks are out of this world!  You are absorbed into the game intantly.  I could go on and on about what makes this game a masterpiece but my words wont do the justice of you actually playing it and experiencing it for yourself.  Buy this game, no BS just a great game well worth every penny.

Playthrough time: 8 hours (a total of 9 hours including the time to get the Jackpot achievement)
+Lovely, totally over the top design - wacky and insane things all over the place
+Good looking graphics
+Works very well with a 360 controller
+Some nice changes of pace like the twin stick space shooter levels
+Good soundtrack
-Somewhat sloppy controls
-A combination of sparse checkpoints and sadistic design makes you replay long sequences
The game is great for using the Xbox 360 controller and playing on the TV from the couch. The game feels like it was made for the 360 controller, so I never played with the keyboard.
The game has low system requirements, so it should run well on most computers. For me it always stuttered for about half a second each time while auto saving, but this was the only issue I encountered.
Hell Yeah starts off with a story just as wacky as the rest of the game. You play as Ash, the skeleton bunny prince of hell, who has gotten private pictures of him bathing with a rubber ducky leaked, so to not seem like a weakling, you have to kill the 100 hell monsters who have seen the pictures.
The game itself is mostly standard platforming. You jump around, avoid obstacles, shoot stuff and navigate the levels to get to the 100 monsters. Each time you encounter one, and get its health down by shooting it or using objects in the environment (depending on the monster) you will get to play a mini-game for a chance to land the killing blow. The mini games are often just matching the right button(s)/get the timing right, but there are a few other ones. There are a lot of different ones, so each one isn't used more than 3, maybe 4 times.
You get to upgrade your health and weapons, and some levels have vehicles: in one you control a submarine, and another one a space ship, and the game turns in to a twin stick shooter. This was quite a nice change of pace.
What the game does best is all the wacky things happening:
I really enjoyed all these things, and I realised that for me, I didn't come back for the gameplay, I came back for all the wackyness. To come around a corner, hear the muffled rap music indicating a shop nearby, enter and hear the full "Money, money gold!" rap parody. The music in the game is very enjoyable and well done.
One design choice I didn't like is that after you stop moving, your character "glides" a bit, which makes it really hard to make certain jumps. You get the jump just right, but when you land at the very small platform, you glide over the edge. This makes the controls not feel very "tight". Combine this with the level design, which has the checkpoints maybe 3-5 minutes between, and some sadistically hard jumps with insta-death spikes if you miss your jump, and I guess that this will send quite a few gamepads airborne and lead to rage quits. When you repeat the same 3-minute section for the 10:th time and have to play it all over again, yet another time. You also have to rewatch any "cutscenes" that appear during that section.
I'm no pro platformer, so there were sections where I had to try many times to get it right, and even though I have lots of patience, I was close to quitting a few times.
So, I wouldn't recommend this game only for the gameplay. It's fine but it has its drawbacks. If you think you would appreciate all the crazy stuff happening, and can ignore the annoying parts, you're up for a good time with Hell Yeah!
